record.title: Stiefel-constrained attention paper attributes CIFAR-10 gain to scale-free optimization step
record.summary: A v3 paper studies Stiefel-constrained query/key projections trained with a corrected Riemannian Adam update. On one CIFAR-10 image-patch benchmark at 10,000 examples, authors report a 6.79 percentage-point gain over AdamW across 12 paired starts; their 12-seed ablation attributes the improvement to a scale-free, step-capped update rather than to the tangent projector or equivariance. The optimizer took 1.82 seconds per epoch versus 0.73 seconds for the baseline. A separate modular-arithmetic grokking experiment finds no benefit for the constrained method; the paper’s positive grokking result is a single-seed pilot and remains unconfirmed. Independent replication and transfer to language-model training are open.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On a CIFAR-10 patch benchmark with 10,000 examples, corrected Stiefel Riemannian Adam improves accuracy by 6.79 percentage points over matched AdamW across 12 paired starts (t=38.33; 12/12 starts).

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A 12-seed ablation attributes a +4.63-point gain to the scale-free step-capped rule and no measured gain to the tangent projector or equivariance. A targeted epsilon sweep reports a 2.6-point loss at epsilon=0.1 (p<0.001).

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report optimizer epoch time of 1.82 seconds versus 0.73 seconds for the baseline, a 2.5× overhead.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In two five-seed modular-arithmetic grokking studies the constrained arm does not outperform the baseline; the claimed stable grokking under slingshot conditions is a single-seed pilot. The paper does not establish benefit on language-model training.

contradictory_evidence: The positive modular-arithmetic grokking signal does not persist: the paper reports reruns reversing the initial single-seed result, two five-seed studies where the constrained arm does not grok better, and no effect-size claim for the pilot.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported paired CIFAR-10 patch result and scale-free-step ablation have not been independently rerun or audited against released code in this review.
Generalization beyond the small image-patch benchmark, especially to language-model attention training, is unknown; measured optimizer epoch overhead is 2.5×.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported paired-seed gain and causal ablation generalize, a scale-free constrained update could improve attention-projection optimization and help explain which geometric component earns an accuracy change. This is notable for training-method design but currently rests on one small image-patch benchmark, has material runtime overhead and no independent replication.
limitations: Results are from one CIFAR-10 image-patch task; language-model or broad vision transfer is untested.
All empirical outcomes are paper-reported; no independent reproduction was conducted.
The corrected optimizer takes 1.82 seconds per epoch versus 0.73 seconds for AdamW, a reported 2.5× overhead.

The earlier fixed-step Riemannian SGD result is mostly explained by orthonormal initialization, while the corrected Adam gain is attributed to the scale-free step; these variants must not be conflated.
Grokking benefit is not established: controlled multi-seed studies find no gain, and the positive slingshot result is a single-seed pilot.

technical.claimed_result: Corrected Stiefel Riemannian Adam gains 6.79 percentage points over matched AdamW at n=10,000 on a CIFAR-10 patch benchmark across 12 paired starts; a 12-seed ablation attributes its gain to the scale-free step. Epoch time is 1.82 s vs 0.73 s.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper supplies a detailed method, proofs of stated geometric properties and reported paired-seed/ablation experiments. This review did not independently reproduce them.
technical.mechanism: Query/key projections are constrained to Stiefel frames; the corrected update uses tangent projection, scalar second moment, step-norm cap and polar retraction. The authors’ ablation says scale-free step earns the observed gain, not projection or equivariance.
technical.regime: CIFAR-10 patch task at n=10k, 12 paired starts, data sweep 1k–50k; modular-arithmetic grokking uses five seeds per arm plus a separate one-seed pilot.
technical.reproducibility: No code or independent run was inspected. Reproduce the 12-start image result and epsilon intervention, then test matched language-model attention tasks.
technical.strongest_baseline: Matched AdamW under the same architecture and training schedule, plus the paper’s component ablation.

brief.title: Stiefel-constrained attention paper attributes CIFAR-10 gain to scale-free optimization step
brief.why_it_matters: The paper asks whether constraining attention query/key projections improves learning and which part of that method earns any gain. Its seed-matched ablation argues that scale-free step normalization, rather than the geometric projector itself, explains the reported CIFAR-10 improvement. The result is narrow and slower to train, and controlled grokking tests are negative, so it is a training-method signal rather than evidence of broad language-model gains.
